summary: Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and served as a professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009).
Prabhasa Dharma (1931–1999) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kyozan Joshu Sasaki in 1967 and Seikō Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1898–1956) was an Indologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Krishnagar Government College, University of Calcutta, and University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, he held professorships at Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.
Pragati Sahni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Damien Keown. She has served as a lecturer at the University of Delhi.

Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. His career included posts at Visva-Bharati, Ravenshaw College, Gangadhar Meher University, Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya, and Utkal University.

Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Georgetown University and the University of Mumbai (PhD 1964). He held posts at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, University of Chicago, and Harvard University.
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD from the University of Mysore (attested 2014).
Pratap Chandra Chunder (1919–2008) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, where he was taught by Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
Pratap Kumar Penumala works in religious studies and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and a visiting professor at Colorado College.

Pratapaditya Pal (born 1935) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and art historian who earned PhDs from the University of Calcutta and Cambridge. He held curatorial and leadership posts at the Museum of Fine Arts Boston, LACMA, and the Art Institute of Chicago.

Prayag Raj Sharma (born 1939) is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Tribhuvan University, including serving as dean at its Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies and as professor (attested 1976–1990).

Prayoon Mererk (born 1955) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi in 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Prayudh Payutto (born 1938) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who graduated from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University in 1962. He served as associate dean there (~1964–1974) and as Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark (1908–1980) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics (~1935–1939), and served in the Office of Strategic Services (~1944–1945).
Priyavrat Sharma (1920–2008) was an Indologist and historian. He served as director at Banaras Hindu University, including heading its Postgraduate Institute of Indian Medicine.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø (born 1944) is an Iranian and Central Asian studies linguist educated at the Sorbonne, University of Oslo, and Mainz. He held posts at Mainz, Columbia University, and Harvard University, where he was Aga Khan Professor (~1991–2015).
Przemysław Szczurek is an Indologist who held posts at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań and at the University of Breslau, where he is attested in 2021 as Professor of Indology.

Pulinbihari Chakravarti was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society (attested 1951).
Punyavijaya (1895–1971) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi and founded the Prakrit Text Society.

Purna Harsha Bajracharya worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 1972, he was attested as Chief Research Officer at both the Archaeological Survey of India and the Department of Archaeology.
